A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Uni-Retrieval study. Their complete 16-page contents, including Tables 1–6, Figures 1–7, equations and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on SER and other datasets, prompt ablations, inference-time measurements and retrieval case studies in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–6 and Figure 4, with experimental details in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same prototype learning module, Prompt Bank, feature extractors, training objectives and inference procedure. No method component or algorithmic step changes.

E1.justification: The evaluated coverage remains SER and the DSR, DomainNet and SketchCOCO datasets reported in Table 6. Query styles, modalities and retrieval scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–4 and the dataset-specific comparisons in Table 6. The newly cited works in Appendix A are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same evaluation metrics, preprocessing, model configurations and training settings, including 20 epochs and batch size 24 per GPU. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Table 5 retains the same prompt-depth and token-count ablations; Table 6 retains the same zero-shot generalization tests. Figure 4 and its retrieval-error analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 42 in Appendix C and retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–6 and the reported qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Uni-Retrieval's SER text-to-image R@1/R@5 remains 83.2/98.7 in Table 1.

T1.justification: The task formulation in Section 2.1 and mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations 1–9 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, proofs or theoretical guarantees are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the STEM retrieval task, SER dataset, Prompt Bank, retrieval performance, efficiency and generalization.

C2.justification: The explanations of performance, prompt-count tradeoffs, retrieval errors and educational applicability are unchanged. The Limitation section also retains the same concerns about broader educational applicability and incorporating professional educational knowledge.

D1.justification: Appendix C is unchanged, including the eight A100 GPUs, optimizer, learning rates, preprocessing and backbone specifications. Implementation documentation and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendices A.2 and A.4 add six cited works: Xiao et al. (2025), Jia et al. (2025a,b), and Zhao et al. (2023, 2024a,b). These supplement existing statements without expanding the related-work argument or changing contribution positioning; no cited works are removed.

P1.justification: v2 identifies only Shuai Zhao as corresponding author, adds his email and shortens numerous bibliography author lists and publication details. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged apart from citation insertions.

P2.justification: The author block changes slightly, bibliography edits alter reference placement, and additional appendix citations cause limited column and page reflow. All seven figures and six tables retain their content, captions and design.

improvement.justification: v2 adds citations and updates author/contact information and bibliography presentation, but the added citations accompany existing statements without new analysis. The method, empirical evidence, reproducibility details and limitations remain unchanged, supporting no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
